ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle DAC=\angle ACB$, $\angle D=86^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BCD$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle DAC = \angle ACB$, \\
it follows that $AD \parallel BC$, \\
hence $\angle D + \angle BCD = 180^\circ$, \\
since $\angle D = 86^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle BCD = 180^\circ - \angle D = 180^\circ - 86^\circ = \boxed{94^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is quadrilateral ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C on the right side slightly above, and D at the upper left; sides AD, DC, CB, BA form the quadrilateral, and diagonal AC is drawn. AC connects A and C, and can be regarded as a transversal intersecting the straight lines AD and BC at the same time. Reasoning: The problem gives ∠DAC = ∠ACB, where ∠DAC is the angle formed by AC and AD, and ∠ACB is the angle formed by AC and BC; these two angles are a pair of alternate interior angles formed by AC cutting AD and BC. Alternate interior angles are equal, so AD ∥ BC. Since AD ∥ BC, side CD is a transversal, so the same-side interior angles ∠D and ∠BCD are supplementary; therefore ∠D + ∠BCD = 180°. Given ∠D = 86°, so ∠BCD = 180° - 86° = 94°.
